issue_context.title: REGR: unhelpful error message with np.min on unordered Categorical
issue_context.body:
xref #28949

on master

```
>>> import numpy as np
>>> import pandas as pd
>>>
>>> pd.__version__
'1.1.0.dev0+1008.g60b0e9fbc'
>>>
>>> cat = pd.Categorical(["a", "b", "c", "b"], ordered=False)
>>> cat
[a, b, c, b]
Categories (3, object): [a, b, c]
>>>
>>> np.min(cat)
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "<stdin>", line 1, in <module>
  File "<__array_function__ internals>", line 6, in amin
  File "C:\Users\simon\Anaconda3\envs\pandas-dev\lib\site-packages\numpy\core\fromnumeric.py", line 2793, in amin
    keepdims=keepdims, initial=initial, where=where)
  File "C:\Users\simon\Anaconda3\envs\pandas-dev\lib\site-packages\numpy\core\fromnumeric.py", line 88, in _wrapreduction
    return reduction(axis=axis, out=out, **passkwargs)
  File "C:\Users\simon\pandas\pandas\util\_decorators.py", line 212, in wrapper
    return func(*args, **kwargs)
TypeError: min() got an unexpected keyword argument 'axis'
```

on 0.25.3

```
>>> import numpy as np
>>> import pandas as pd
>>>
>>> pd.__version__
'0.25.3'
>>>
>>> cat = pd.Categorical(["a", "b", "c", "b"], ordered=False)
>>> cat
[a, b, c, b]
Categories (3, object): [a, b, c]
>>>
>>> np.min(cat)
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "<stdin>", line 1, in <module>
  File "C:\Users\simon\Anaconda3\lib\site-packages\numpy\core\fromnumeric.py", line 2618, in amin
    initial=initial)
  File "C:\Users\simon\Anaconda3\lib\site-packages\numpy\core\fromnumeric.py", line 84, in _wrapreduction
    return reduction(axis=axis, out=out, **passkwargs)
  File "C:\Users\simon\Anaconda3\lib\site-packages\pandas\core\arrays\categorical.py", line 2278, in min
    self.check_for_ordered("min")
  File "C:\Users\simon\Anaconda3\lib\site-packages\pandas\core\arrays\categorical.py", line 1586, in check_for_ordered
    "Categorical to an ordered one\n".format(op=op)
TypeError: Categorical is not ordered for operation min
you can use .as_ordered() to change the Categorical to an ordered one
```
comments:
regression caused by #27929  (between 0.25.3 and 1.0)

37526c1ddbe0952dffe16ac0fe158a00aa7b397f is the first bad commit
commit 37526c1ddbe0952dffe16ac0fe158a00aa7b397f
Author: Mak Sze Chun <makszechun@gmail.com>
Date:   Mon Dec 2 18:37:11 2019 +0800

    API/DEPR: Change default skipna behaviour + deprecate numeric_only in Categorical.min and max (#27929)

cc @makbigc

I'm leaning on that this is more a bug in numpy.

numpy does in ``core/fromnumeric.py::_wrapreduction``:

```python
    return reduction(axis=axis, out=out, **passkwargs)
```

i.e. forcing parameters axis=None and out=None down to our function, requiring us to have those parameters also. Seems to make better sense to push axis and out into the ``passkwargs`` dict, but drop them there if they're None so downstream would not require axis and out parameters?

Of course that's beyond pandas to fix (and I may misunderstand ``_wrapreduction`` of course), and  I agree that ``np.min(cat)`` should work, so I'm ok with doing a fix for this in pandas.

review_comments: IMO adding kwargs just lets users pass wrong arguments and let things fail silently. I'd prefer not passing kwargs and fail hard if wrong argument passed.
added a TODO to capture this suggestion. this PR is a regression fix to be backported. Only minimal changes to restore previous behaviour for now, avoiding code changes/enhancements.

Ok, then I think a good idea would be to check the kwargs using ``pandas.compat.numpy.function.validate_min``. This checks that ``kwargs={"axis": None}`` is accepted, but ``kwargs={"axis": 1}`` fails. Similarly for other args/kwargs.
yes i agree, we check these elsewhere when we pass kwargs
separate PR or here? if here backport the additional code or keep the signature the same as prior to the change that caused the regression?
I think it good to do it here: The kwargs are introduced in this PR, so is reasonable to validate it in the same PR.

> The kwargs are introduced in this PR

not entirely true. The removal of kwargs caused a regression. the removal is reverted here. the working code did not validate the kwargs.

> I think it good to do it here

will do. can decide what to backport at a later date.
